_: Several wordings per court result (say.js; Reigns' fresh deck): the realm never says the same thing twice in a row. Keys are kind.option; {names} are filled by the court. Add a wording to any list to widen it; a key with none uses the court's own line.
grain.order: By royal command, {donor} feeds the starving of {house}, and resents every sack.
{donor}'s granaries open on the King's word. The carts roll to {house}, and {donor} counts each one.
The King makes {donor} feed {house}. {house} eats; {donor} keeps the bill in its head.
{donor} sends grain to {house}, because the King said so. Nobody in {donor}'s hall says thank you.
Wagons of {donor}'s wheat reach {house}'s hungry. {donor}'s steward calls it theft with a seal on it.
grain.grant: Royal grain rolls out of Kingsmere for {house}. The bakers there light their ovens again.
The King opens his own stores for {house}. Tonight, {house}'s children eat.
Kingsmere's granary feeds {house} this winter. Its lord will remember who did.
grain.refuse: The King refuses grain. In {house}'s lands, the bannermen begin to talk.
No grain for {house}. Its bannermen eat their seed corn and wonder aloud what a King is for.
The King keeps his granaries shut. {house} tightens its belt, and its bannermen loosen their tongues.
{house} goes hungry by the King's word. Its knights start asking who else might feed them.
informer.reward: {informer} leaves court with a heavier purse. Within the month, {suspect} knows who talked.
The King pays {informer} for the tale. {suspect} hears of it before the coins are spent.
{informer} is rewarded in silver. Court is a small place: {suspect} soon knows whose silver.
Gold for {informer}, a long memory for {suspect}. The two no longer dine at the same table.
informer.dismiss: The King dismisses the accusation. {informer} leaves court red-faced.
"Gossip," says the King. {informer} bows very low, red to the ears.
The King hears {informer} out, and laughs. The court laughs with him. {informer} does not.
The accusation is thrown out. {suspect} sends {informer} a cask of wine, which is worse than a blade.
remembers.hear: The King hears {name} out and promises nothing. {house} goes home with its grudge, and it grows.
{name} speaks; the King listens; nothing is promised. {house} rides home angrier than it came.
The King nods through all of it and offers nothing. {name} has heard kinder silence from a wall.
"We will think on it," says the King. {house} has heard that before. The grudge gets heavier.
{name} is heard to the end, and sent away with nothing. {house}'s old wound opens a little wider.
remembers.purse: {house} sends {gold} gold to Kingsmere. {name} had hoped for thanks, not a bill.
The King answers {name}'s complaint with an invoice: {gold} gold. {house} pays, and seethes.
{name} came for an apology and leaves {gold} gold lighter. {house} will tell this story for years.
{gold} gold from {house} to the crown, for the trouble of listening. {name} pays with a smile like a knife.
remembers.firm: "The crown did what it must." {name} bows, and adds it to the account.
The King stands by what was done. {name} bows, and {house} adds a line to its long ledger.
"It was right then and it's right now," says the King. {name} says nothing, which says enough.
The King gives no ground. {name} leaves, already counting what the crown will owe for it.
council.side: The King sides with {winner}. {loser} leaves the council hall without bowing.
The King's word goes to {winner}. {loser}'s lords push back their chairs and walk out.
{winner} has the King's backing. {loser} hears it with a face like stone, and is gone before the wine.
The council ends with {winner} smiling. {loser} slams the door hard enough to shake the tapestries.
The King rules for {winner}. {loser} doesn't argue; it just stops coming to council.
